questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements (I-III) regarding excretory products and their elimination:

Statement I: Protonephridia or flame cells are excretory structures in Platyhelminthes such as Planaria.

Statement II: Nephridia are tubular excretory structures found in earthworms and other annelids.

Statement III: Malpighian tubules serve as the excretory structures of most insects, including cockroaches.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Platyhelminthes Excretory Structure
In flatworms like Planaria, protonephridia (flame cells) function in excretion and osmoregulation, verifying the accuracy of the proposition regarding flatworms.

Step 2: Evaluation of Annelid Excretory Structure
Earthworms and other annelids possess segmentally arranged tubular nephridia that eliminate nitrogenous waste and maintain fluid balance, confirming the accuracy of the proposition regarding annelids.

Step 3: Evaluation of Insect Excretory Structure
Cockroaches and most insects possess Malpighian tubules opening into the gut to clear waste and regulate water balance, confirming the proposition regarding insects.

Final Conceptual Answer: The propositions regarding protonephridia in flatworms, nephridia in annelids, and Malpighian tubules in insects are all biologically correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_EXCRETORY_PRODUCTS_AND_THEIR_ELIMINATION_STATEMENT_BASED_3_Q02 - Ureotelism and site of urea production

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements (I-III) regarding excretory products and their elimination:

Statement I: Mammals, many terrestrial amphibians, and marine fishes are predominantly ureotelic animals.

Statement II: Ammonia produced by metabolism is converted into urea in the liver of ureotelic animals.

Statement III: Human kidneys synthesize urea directly from uric acid inside the renal pelvis.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Ureotelic Animals Distribution
Terrestrial adaptation favored less toxic wastes like urea for water conservation; mammals, adult terrestrial amphibians, and marine fishes are ureotelic, confirming the first proposition.

Step 2: Evaluation of Hepatic Urea Synthesis
Toxic ammonia generated by deamination is transported to the liver, where it is biochemically transformed into urea and released into the blood, confirming the second proposition.

Step 3: Evaluation of Renal Pelvis Function
The kidneys filter and excrete urea from blood; they do not synthesize urea from uric acid, and the renal pelvis is simply a funnel-shaped collection basin leading into the ureter, making the third proposition incorrect.

Final Conceptual Answer: Ureotelism in mammals and amphibians as well as hepatic urea synthesis are biologically correct, whereas urea synthesis does not occur in the renal pelvis from uric acid.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_EXCRETORY_PRODUCTS_AND_THEIR_ELIMINATION_STATEMENT_BASED_3_Q03 - Anatomical landmarks and internal zonation of kidney

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements (I-III) regarding excretory products and their elimination:

Statement I: The human kidneys are bean-shaped structures situated between the levels of the last thoracic and third lumbar vertebrae.

Statement II: Towards the centre of the inner concave surface of the kidney is a notch called the hilum through which ureters, vessels, and nerves enter.

Statement III: The renal cortex extends in between the medullary pyramids as renal columns called Columns of Bertini.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Kidney Vertebral Position
Human kidneys lie retroperitoneally between the levels of T12 and L3 vertebrae close to the dorsal abdominal wall, verifying the first proposition.

Step 2: Evaluation of Hilum Anatomy
The inner concave margin bears a central indentation termed the hilum through which the ureter, renal artery, renal vein, lymphatics, and nerves pass, verifying the second proposition.

Step 3: Evaluation of Columns of Bertini
Inward projections of cortical tissue penetrating between the conical medullary pyramids form the renal columns of Bertini, verifying the third proposition.

Final Conceptual Answer: The propositions regarding kidney position between T12 and L3, presence of the hilum, and cortical Columns of Bertini are all factually correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_EXCRETORY_PRODUCTS_AND_THEIR_ELIMINATION_STATEMENT_BASED_3_Q04 - Structural comparison of cortical and juxtamedullary nephrons

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements (I-III) regarding excretory products and their elimination:

Statement I: In cortical nephrons, the loop of Henle is short and extends only very little into the medulla.

Statement II: In juxtamedullary nephrons, the loop of Henle is very long and runs deep into the medulla.

Statement III: The vasa recta is highly developed and prominent in cortical nephrons but completely absent in juxtamedullary nephrons.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Cortical Nephron Henle Loop
Cortical nephrons constitute the majority of nephrons and possess short loops of Henle dipping minimally into the outer medulla, confirming the first proposition.

Step 2: Evaluation of Juxtamedullary Nephron Henle Loop
Juxtamedullary nephrons have corpuscles near the corticomedullary junction and possess long Henle's loops descending deep into the inner medulla, confirming the second proposition.

Step 3: Evaluation of Vasa Recta Distribution
Vasa recta are hairpin capillaries running parallel to long loops of Henle in juxtamedullary nephrons; in cortical nephrons, vasa recta are absent or highly reduced, rendering the third proposition incorrect.

Final Conceptual Answer: Short Henle loops in cortical nephrons and long loops in juxtamedullary nephrons are correct, whereas vasa recta are absent or reduced in cortical nephrons and well-developed in juxtamedullary nephrons.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_EXCRETORY_PRODUCTS_AND_THEIR_ELIMINATION_STATEMENT_BASED_3_Q05 - Glomerular blood perfusion and daily filtration volumes

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements (I-III) regarding excretory products and their elimination:

Statement I: On an average, 1100-1200 mL of blood is filtered by the human kidneys per minute.

Statement II: Glomerular filtration rate (GFR) in a healthy individual is approximately 125 mL/minute, which equals 180 litres per day.

Statement III: A healthy adult human excretes approximately 180 litres of urine per day.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Renal Blood Flow
Both kidneys receive 1100 to 1200 mL of blood each minute, constituting roughly one-fifth of the cardiac output, confirming the first proposition.

Step 2: Evaluation of Daily GFR Volume
The normal glomerular filtration rate is 125 mL/min, which calculates to 180 litres of filtrate produced per day, confirming the second proposition.

Step 3: Evaluation of Daily Urine Excretion
Approximately 99% of the 180 litres of filtrate is reabsorbed, resulting in only about 1.5 litres of urine excreted daily; excreting 180 litres of urine would be fatal dehydration, making the third proposition incorrect.

Final Conceptual Answer: Renal blood flow of 1100-1200 mL/min and daily GFR of 180 L are correct, whereas human urine output is approximately 1.5 litres per day rather than 180 litres.

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements (I-III) regarding excretory products and their elimination:

Statement I: The epithelial cells of Bowman's capsule called podocytes are arranged intricately to leave minute spaces called filtration slits.

Statement II: Almost all constituents of plasma except proteins pass across the filtration membrane into the lumen of Bowman's capsule.

Statement III: Glomerular capillary blood pressure causes filtration of blood through three distinct layers forming the filtration membrane.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Podocyte Slit Pores
Podocytes form the visceral layer of Bowman's capsule, extending pedicels that interdigitate to create filtration slits (slit pores), confirming the first proposition.

Step 2: Evaluation of Filtrate Solute Selectivity
Due to size and negative charge barriers, large plasma proteins are retained while water and crystalloids filter through, confirming the second proposition.

Step 3: Evaluation of Hydrostatic Filtration Driving Force
Glomerular capillary hydrostatic pressure forces fluid across the fenestrated endothelium, basement membrane, and podocyte layer, confirming the third proposition.

Final Conceptual Answer: Podocyte filtration slits, protein exclusion from filtrate, and blood pressure as the driving filtration force are all biologically correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_EXCRETORY_PRODUCTS_AND_THEIR_ELIMINATION_STATEMENT_BASED_3_Q07 - Bulk reabsorption and histology of proximal tubule

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements (I-III) regarding excretory products and their elimination:

Statement I: Nearly all essential nutrients are reabsorbed by the proximal convoluted tubule (PCT).

Statement II: Approximately 70-80 per cent of electrolytes and water are reabsorbed by the PCT.

Statement III: The PCT is lined by simple cuboidal brush border epithelium which increases the surface area for reabsorption.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Nutrient Reabsorption in PCT
The proximal convoluted tubule reclaims virtually 100% of filtered glucose and amino acids by secondary active transport, confirming the first proposition.

Step 2: Evaluation of Water and Electrolyte Reabsorption in PCT
Approximately 70 to 80% of sodium, potassium, bicarbonate, chloride, and water are reabsorbed along the PCT, confirming the second proposition.

Step 3: Evaluation of PCT Epithelial Brush Border
The luminal surface of the PCT features simple cuboidal cells with densely arrayed microvilli (brush border) that dramatically increase absorptive area, confirming the third proposition.

Final Conceptual Answer: Complete nutrient reabsorption, 70-80% electrolyte reabsorption, and brush border lining of the proximal tubule are all biologically correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_EXCRETORY_PRODUCTS_AND_THEIR_ELIMINATION_STATEMENT_BASED_3_Q08 - Permeability of Henle loop limbs and filtrate tonicity

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements (I-III) regarding excretory products and their elimination:

Statement I: The descending limb of the loop of Henle is permeable to water but almost impermeable to electrolytes.

Statement II: The ascending limb of the loop of Henle is impermeable to water but allows transport of electrolytes actively or passively.

Statement III: The filtrate becomes progressively diluted as it moves down the descending limb and concentrated as it moves up the ascending limb.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Descending Limb Properties
The descending limb permits osmotic exit of water into the hypertonic medulla while restricting solute movement, confirming the first proposition.

Step 2: Evaluation of Ascending Limb Properties
The ascending limb does not allow water to exit, while sodium and chloride are extruded passively in the thin segment and actively in the thick segment, confirming the second proposition.

Step 3: Evaluation of Directional Tonicity Changes
Water loss in the descending limb concentrates the filtrate towards the hairpin loop, whereas solute loss without water in the ascending limb dilutes the filtrate towards the cortex; the third proposition inverts these physiological changes and is therefore incorrect.

Final Conceptual Answer: Water permeability of the descending limb and electrolyte transport by the ascending limb are correct, whereas filtrate becomes concentrated descending the loop and diluted ascending the loop.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_EXCRETORY_PRODUCTS_AND_THEIR_ELIMINATION_STATEMENT_BASED_3_Q09 - Excretory structures in crustaceans and annelids

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements (I-III) regarding excretory products and their elimination:

Statement I: Antennal glands or green glands perform the excretory function in crustaceans like prawns.

Statement II: Protonephridia or flame cells are complex multicellular organs found exclusively in mammalian kidneys.

Statement III: Nephridia help to remove nitrogenous wastes and maintain fluid and ionic balance in earthworms.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Crustacean Excretory Glands
Crustaceans like prawns possess specialized antennal glands (also called green glands) located at the base of the antennae for excretion, confirming the first proposition.

Step 2: Evaluation of Protonephridia Distribution
Protonephridia (flame cells) are primitive tubular units found in invertebrates like flatworms and rotifers, not complex organs in mammals, making the second proposition incorrect.

Step 3: Evaluation of Annelid Nephridia
Earthworms and other annelids rely on segmentally repeated nephridia to eliminate metabolic wastes and preserve osmotic balance, confirming the third proposition.

Final Conceptual Answer: Antennal glands in crustaceans and nephridia in earthworms are correct, whereas flame cells are primitive invertebrate structures rather than mammalian organs.

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements (I-III) regarding excretory products and their elimination:

Statement I: Renin is an enzyme synthesized and released by the adrenal medulla in response to acute hypertension.

Statement II: Angiotensin II is a powerful vasoconstrictor that increases glomerular blood pressure and GFR.

Statement III: Aldosterone causes reabsorption of Na+ and water from the distal parts of the tubule.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Renin Production Site and Trigger
Renin is produced by juxtaglomerular (JG) cells in the kidney in response to a fall in GFR or blood pressure, not by the adrenal medulla during hypertension, making the first proposition incorrect.

Step 2: Evaluation of Angiotensin II Vasoconstrictive Action
Angiotensin II acts directly on vascular smooth muscle to constrict arterioles, raising systemic pressure and restoring glomerular filtration pressure, confirming the second proposition.

Step 3: Evaluation of Aldosterone Tubular Action
Aldosterone, secreted by the adrenal cortex, acts on the distal convoluted tubule and collecting duct to stimulate sodium and water retention, confirming the third proposition.

Final Conceptual Answer: Vasoconstriction by angiotensin II and distal sodium reabsorption by aldosterone are correct, whereas renin is secreted by renal juxtaglomerular cells in response to low blood pressure.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_EXCRETORY_PRODUCTS_AND_THEIR_ELIMINATION_STATEMENT_BASED_3_Q11 - Counter current patterns and urine concentration factor

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements (I-III) regarding excretory products and their elimination:

Statement I: Human kidneys can produce urine that is nearly twenty times more concentrated than the initial filtrate formed.

Statement II: The flow of filtrate in the two limbs of Henle's loop is in opposite directions and forms a counter current.

Statement III: The flow of blood through the two limbs of vasa recta is in a counter current pattern.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Maximum Urine Concentrating Capacity
Mammalian kidneys can concentrate urine up to about 1200 mOsmol L⁻¹ from an initial filtrate of 300 mOsmol L⁻¹, which is four times more concentrated, not twenty times, making the first proposition incorrect.

Step 2: Evaluation of Tubular Counter Current Flow
Fluid descends in the descending limb and ascends in the ascending limb of Henle's loop, creating opposing flow directions termed a counter current, confirming the second proposition.

Step 3: Evaluation of Vascular Counter Current Flow
Blood descends in the descending limb of the vasa recta and ascends in the ascending limb, creating a parallel counter current exchanger, confirming the third proposition.

Final Conceptual Answer: Opposing counter current flows in Henle's loop and vasa recta are correct, whereas kidneys can concentrate urine four times above initial filtrate rather than twenty times.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_EXCRETORY_PRODUCTS_AND_THEIR_ELIMINATION_STATEMENT_BASED_3_Q12 - Atrial natriuretic factor mechanism and hemodynamics

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements (I-III) regarding excretory products and their elimination:

Statement I: Atrial Natriuretic Factor (ANF) stimulates juxtaglomerular cells to release renin to elevate systemic blood pressure.

Statement II: An increase in blood flow to the atria of the heart causes the release of Atrial Natriuretic Factor (ANF).

Statement III: ANF causes vasodilation of blood vessels and thereby decreases blood pressure, acting as a check on RAAS.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of ANF Influence on Renin
ANF inhibits renin secretion and counteracts the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone axis; it does not stimulate renin release, making the first proposition incorrect.

Step 2: Evaluation of ANF Secretory Trigger
Elevated venous return or high blood volume stretches the cardiac atria, stimulating myocytes to secrete ANF into the circulation, confirming the second proposition.

Step 3: Evaluation of ANF Physiological Function
ANF promotes vascular smooth muscle relaxation (vasodilation) and natriuresis, lowering blood pressure and acting as a negative check on the renin-angiotensin system, confirming the third proposition.

Final Conceptual Answer: Atrial stretch causing ANF secretion and ANF-induced vasodilation are correct, whereas ANF acts as a check on the renin-angiotensin system rather than stimulating renin.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_EXCRETORY_PRODUCTS_AND_THEIR_ELIMINATION_STATEMENT_BASED_3_Q13 - Volume, pH, and urea excretion in normal human urine

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements (I-III) regarding excretory products and their elimination:

Statement I: An adult human excretes, on an average, 1 to 1.5 litres of urine per day.

Statement II: Normal human urine is a strongly basic watery fluid with an average pH of 8.5 to 9.0.

Statement III: On an average, 25-30 grams of urea is excreted out per day by an adult human.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Daily Urine Volume
A healthy adult human voids between 1.0 and 1.5 litres of urine daily under typical hydration conditions, confirming the first proposition.

Step 2: Evaluation of Normal Urine pH
Urine is slightly acidic with an average pH of approximately 6.0 due to active secretion of hydrogen ions; it is not strongly basic, making the second proposition incorrect.

Step 3: Evaluation of Daily Urea Excretion
A healthy human consuming a standard diet eliminates approximately 25 to 30 grams of urea each day in urine, confirming the third proposition.

Final Conceptual Answer: Daily excretion of 1 to 1.5 litres of urine and 25-30 grams of urea are correct, whereas normal urine is slightly acidic with an average pH of 6.0.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_EXCRETORY_PRODUCTS_AND_THEIR_ELIMINATION_STATEMENT_BASED_3_Q14 - Disorders of the human excretory system

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements (I-III) regarding excretory products and their elimination:

Statement I: During hemodialysis, the cleared blood is pumped back to the body through a vein after adding anti-heparin.

Statement II: Renal calculi are caused by pathogenic viral colonies multiplying within the lumen of the collecting ducts.

Statement III: Glomerulonephritis is a clinical condition characterized by the inflammation of the glomeruli of the kidney.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Hemodialysis Blood Return Protocol
After urea diffuses across the dialyzer membrane into the dialysing fluid, anti-heparin is added to the blood to restore normal coagulation before it is infused into a vein, confirming the first proposition.

Step 2: Evaluation of Renal Calculi Pathology
Renal calculi are insoluble stones formed by the precipitation and crystallization of mineral salts (primarily oxalates) within the kidney, not viral infections, making the second proposition incorrect.

Step 3: Evaluation of Glomerulonephritis Definition
Glomerulonephritis refers specifically to inflammatory changes affecting the glomerular capillary tufts in the renal cortex, confirming the third proposition.

Final Conceptual Answer: Anti-heparin addition before venous return during hemodialysis and glomerulonephritis as glomeruli inflammation are correct, whereas renal calculi are mineral stones rather than viral colonies.
